data.narrative:
HLabs is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Paul Hetherington that has raised $5M+. The valuation analysis draws on a broader comp universe of 9 peers—1 public (277810.KQ) and 8 private firms including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI—though a tight peer set at identical stage and valuation tier is limited.

Stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable method, using the $5M total raised as a baseline proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage transitions in the sector. This yields an implied valuation of $12.5M. A peer-median approach was not feasible; while 10 robotics and manufacturing companies exist in the reference universe, fewer than three comparable datapoints could be isolated at the same stage, adjacent stages, or similar valuation tiers, making cross-sectional comparison unreliable.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $11M to $14M, with a median of $12M. This range reflects the step-up multiple applied to confirmed capital raised, discounted and elevated by ±15% to account for stage-specific variance. Key uncertainties include the absence of multiple methodological confirmation and sparse early-stage comparable data within the robotics subsector, which limits confidence in the precision of the range. The valuation should be revisited once additional seed or early-growth stage comparable transactions are available.
